templates.name: Project kickoff agenda and run sheet
templates.purpose: Runs the Project Atlas kickoff (milestone M01, Monday 12 October 2026) that launches the 12-month program with the sponsor, workstream leads, regional HR leads and Legal. It sets out preparation, a timed three-hour plenary agenda, sponsor lines, breakout prompts, the on-the-day run sheet and the outputs the PMO must capture before the charter goes to the steering committee on 23 October 2026 (M02).
templates.audience: HR Program Manager (runs it); Chief People Officer (sponsor and opener); the six workstream leads (WS1 to WS6); cross-cutting leads for country implementation, legal review, change and communications, and the PMO (CC1 to CC4); regional HR leads (Americas, EMEA, APAC); country HR leads in all 13 jurisdictions; observers from Internal Audit, the SOX PMO, Trade Compliance and the Privacy Office.
templates.when: Preparation from T-10 business days (28 September 2026); plenary on 12 October 2026, 07:00 to 10:00 Pacific; APAC session on 13 October 2026, 09:00 Taipei and Shanghai time; follow-up within 2 business days.
templates.owner: Program management office (CC4), with HR Change and Communications (CC3)

items.text: Send the calendar hold for 12 October 2026, 07:00 to 10:00 Pacific, with the video link, the HQ room and a dial-in number; send a separate hold for the APAC session on 13 October at 09:00 Taipei time.

Confirm attendance: the sponsor, all six workstream leads and their deputies, the four cross-cutting leads, the three regional HR leads, a country HR lead for each of the 13 jurisdictions, and the Internal Audit, SOX PMO, Trade Compliance and Privacy Office observers.
items.detail: If a workstream lead cannot attend, their deputy attends with authority to commit time and name owners.

items.text: Preload the Master checklist with all 438 items (57 policies, 97 processes, 284 legal obligations), each with a provisional workstream, provisional owner role and tier from the catalog.
Give every attendee access to Project HQ, Plan, Approvals, RAID log and Master checklist, and test that each workstream lead can filter the Master checklist to their own items.
Circulate the pre-read: charter draft v0.9, plan on a page (waves W0 to W4 and milestones M01 to M18), the approval chain summary and the link to video V1 'Project Atlas in 90 seconds'.
Build the deck: why now, scope and numbers, waves and milestones, the five stages and definition of done, approval chains, country gates, governance and cadence, and the asks.
items.detail: No more than 20 slides; every number must match project-core and the Master checklist.

items.text: Brief the sponsor for 30 minutes: the three messages, the asks of leads, and the likely objections (capacity during year-end close and compensation review, local consultation timelines).
Set up the RAID log with sections for kickoff decisions, actions, risks and a parking lot so the scribe can capture live.
Assign breakout rooms by workstream, name a facilitator and a note taker for each, and send them the breakout prompts.

Check the date against local calendars: 12 October 2026 is after the Israeli autumn holidays and before Diwali (around 8 November 2026) (verify both), and there is no national holiday in the other 12 jurisdictions that day except where local HR says otherwise.

sections.title: Plenary agenda: 12 October 2026, 07:00 to 10:00 Pacific
sections.intro: Times are Pacific. On 12 October 2026 that is 16:00 Berlin, 17:00 Tel Aviv, 19:30 Bengaluru, 22:00 Taipei and Shanghai, 21:00 Hanoi, 10:00 Toronto and Raleigh, 09:00 Austin and 08:00 Denver.

items.text: 07:00-07:10 Welcome, purpose of the session and ways of working: questions go in chat, the scribe logs decisions, actions and risks live in the RAID log, and parked items are answered within 2 business days.

07:10-07:25 Why Atlas and why now: 438 items across 13 jurisdictions; what goes wrong without them (rules that cannot be enforced locally, missing SOX and Nasdaq evidence, inconsistent manager practice, audit findings); what success looks like on 8 October 2027.

07:25-07:50 Scope, waves and milestones: Mobilize to 6 November 2026; Wave 1 from 9 November 2026 to 12 February 2027; Wave 2 to 14 May 2027; Wave 3 to 13 August 2027; Wave 4 to 8 October 2027; freezes 21 December to 1 January and 5 to 14 February. Walk the Plan page.
items.detail: Highlight the gate milestones: M02 charter (23 Oct), M04 baseline (6 Nov), M07 Wave 1 approvals (29 Jan), M08 Wave 1 live (12 Feb), M11 (14 May), M14 all required items live (13 Aug), M16 audit readiness (24 Sep), M18 close (8 Oct 2027).

items.text: 07:50-08:10 How every item moves: Discover (2 weeks), Draft (3), Review (2), Approve (2), Go live (1); the definition of done for each stage; the standard templates used at each stage.
items.detail: Show where this toolkit fits: T-PM-BASELINE in Mobilize, T-PM-WORKSHOP in Discover, T-POLICY in Draft, T-PM-POLICY-REVIEW in Review, T-PM-APPROVAL-RECORD in Approve, T-PM-COUNTRY-LAUNCH and T-PM-LAUNCH-COMMS in Go live.
items.owner: HR Program Manager and Employment counsel

items.text: 08:10-08:25 Approval chains: the five default chains (global policy, process document, legal obligation, public company and semiconductor control, project document); named approvers are needed for every step by 30 October 2026 (M03). Demo an approval on the Approvals page.

08:35-08:55 Country implementation and local gates: works council co-determination in Germany, democratic procedure in China, internal labor regulation registration in Vietnam, work rules filing and labor-management meetings in Taiwan, standing orders and bilingual displays in India, Hebrew versions in Israel, French for any Quebec-based staff; how lead times feed the Plan.
08:55-09:30 Workstream breakouts (six rooms) using the breakout prompts below.
items.detail: Regional HR leads and Employment counsel move between rooms. Each room produces: confirmed scope, owner gaps, top three risks, candidate Wave 1 items and capacity concerns.

items.text: 09:30-09:45 Readouts: each workstream lead has 2 minutes for owners confirmed, biggest risk and one ask.

09:45-09:55 Governance and cadence: weekly status report (published Fridays), workstream stand-ups, monthly steering committee plus gate meetings, RAID log discipline, change control after plan v1.0 (T-PM-CHANGE-REQUEST), time commitments.
09:55-10:00 Close: decisions made, actions and owners, next dates (charter to steering committee 23 October, approvers named 30 October, baseline complete 6 November).

sections.title: Sponsor opening lines
sections.intro: The sponsor delivers these in the 07:10 block, adapted to their own words.

items.text: Thank you for being here. Project Atlas has one goal: every HR policy, process and legal obligation we have documented, approved, live and owned in all 13 jurisdictions by 8 October 2027.
Today we have 438 items. Some are well documented, some live in one person's inbox, and some don't exist yet. In 12 months every one will have an owner, a current version, a review date and evidence.

This is not a writing exercise. A rule that hasn't been through the works council in Germany, democratic procedure in China, filing in Taiwan or registration in Vietnam can't be relied on there, so local launch is part of done.
I'm asking each workstream lead for [x] hours a week and each owner to treat their Atlas items as part of their job, not extra to it. I will clear conflicts with your leaders.
Raise risks early. A red status in week 3 is useful; a surprise in week 12 is not.

sections.title: Breakout prompts (35 minutes)
sections.intro: The room facilitator keeps to time and the note taker records answers in the RAID log or a shared sheet linked from Project HQ.

items.text: Which items in your workstream would worry you most if an auditor or regulator asked for them tomorrow?
items.detail: List item ids. These are candidate Wave 1 items for the baseline.

items.text: Who actually owns each item today, and which role should own it after October 2027?
items.detail: Flag items with no owner or disputed ownership; the workstream lead resolves them by 23 October.

items.text: Where do the current documents live (Darwinbox, intranet, SharePoint, Confluence, LMS, local drives, email), and who can collect them by 30 October?
Which items depend on another workstream or a cross-cutting team, such as Legal, Country implementation or Communications?
What capacity do you really have between now and 18 December, given year-end close, the compensation cycle and holidays?
items.detail: Capture as hours per week per role. Gaps go to the RAID log as resource risks.

items.text: Which country gates (consultation, filing, translation) touch your likely Wave 1 items, and how long do they take?
Open the bridge at 06:45 Pacific; host and co-host admit attendees, test screen share, live captions and breakout rooms.
At 07:00 announce that the session is recorded and why, and offer to pause recording for any discussion; store the recording on Project HQ with access limited to the program team for 90 days.
items.detail: California requires consent of all parties to record confidential communications (Penal Code 632); give the GDPR notice for German attendees and the equivalent notice elsewhere.

items.text: Scribe captures decisions, actions (owner role and due date) and risks directly in the RAID log during the session, not afterwards.
Timekeeper gives a 5-minute warning at the end of each block and moves parked topics to the parking lot.
Open breakout rooms at 08:55 with pre-assigned attendees; regional HR leads and Employment counsel join rooms on request.
Read back the parking lot at 09:55 and assign an owner to each item.
Run the 60-minute APAC session on 13 October at 09:00 Taipei and Shanghai (08:00 Hanoi): sponsor video clip, waves and stages, country gates, and a Q&A led by the APAC regional HR lead.
Decisions made
items.detail: Each decision logged in the RAID log with a decision id (D01 onwards), owner role and date.

items.text: Actions
items.detail: Owner role, due date and status; reviewed at the first weekly status on 16 October 2026.

items.text: Risks and issues raised
items.detail: Logged with likelihood, impact and owner; resourcing and capacity risks flagged for the charter.

items.text: Workstream leads and deputies confirmed
items.detail: One row per WS1 to WS6 and CC1 to CC4.

items.text: Approver nominations per chain step
items.detail: Due 30 October 2026 (M03); missing nominations escalate to the sponsor on 27 October.

items.text: Country gate lead-time inputs
items.detail: Per jurisdiction: consultation body, filing or registration, languages, realistic lead time in weeks. Due from regional HR leads by 21 October for the charter.

items.text: Send the kickoff summary within 1 business day: decisions, actions, recording link, next dates and the link to the baseline form.
Update Project HQ, the Plan and the Master checklist with confirmed leads, owners and any scope notes.
Send a 3-question feedback pulse: clarity of goals (1 to 5), clarity of my role (1 to 5), biggest concern (free text).

notes: The kickoff is for commitment, not information. Leave with named leads, deputies, approvers and time commitments; without them Mobilize slips and the 6 November baseline gate fails.
Send the charter draft and plan on a page as a pre-read and keep slides short, so the plenary is spent on scope questions, risks and breakouts.
Show each workstream its own list in the Master checklist. Seeing 60 to 90 named items makes the scale real in a way that totals do not.
No single slot works for 13 jurisdictions. Record the plenary, run a separate APAC session and give India a local follow-up, rather than asking APAC staff to join at 22:00.
Don't promise local launch dates at the kickoff. Country gate lead times come from the regional HR leads and go into the charter and Plan at M02.
Log everything live in the RAID log so the first weekly status report on 16 October already shows kickoff decisions, actions and risks.

countryNotes.us: No consultation duty applies. Bring the SOX PMO and Stock Administration into the WS4 breakout because many Wave 1 public-company items (clawback, Section 16, insider trading controls) sit in the US, and keep program messages consistent with NLRA Section 7 rights.
countryNotes.us-ca: Announce recording at the start: California requires all-party consent to record confidential communications (Penal Code 632). Invite the HQ HRBP, since California items with fixed dates, such as the SB 294 notice by 1 February, are early Wave 1 candidates.
countryNotes.us-co: Include the Colorado site HR contact in the WS1 and WS2 breakouts: pay transparency posting and promotion notices (C.R.S. 8-5-201) and the POWR Act carry per-violation penalties and are likely Wave 1 items.
countryNotes.us-nc: Include the North Carolina site HR contact. Flag early that any policy change reducing pay, PTO or bonus terms needs written notice at least one full pay period before it takes effect (G.S. 95-25.13).
countryNotes.us-tx: Include the Texas site HR contact. Texas has few state-specific items, so it can serve as a pilot site for US launch sequencing.
countryNotes.us-wa: The kickoff itself is fine, but later employee meetings about the program must stay off political, religious and union topics, which RCW 49.44.250 makes voluntary. Invite Washington HR because session laws often change requirements mid-year.
countryNotes.ca: Invite Toronto and Vancouver HR. Brief them on the Ontario written-policy duties at 25+ employees (disconnecting from work, electronic monitoring) and confirm whether any Quebec-based remote staff need French versions (Bill 96).
countryNotes.de: Inform the works council chair about the program before or at the kickoff and offer a separate briefing; early information under §80(2) BetrVG avoids later delays on co-determined items (§87). Get consent before recording German attendees and give a GDPR notice.
countryNotes.il: The Israeli work week runs Sunday to Thursday and 12 October 2026 falls after the autumn holidays (verify). Plan a short Hebrew summary for the local team and allow for reserve-duty absences in capacity planning.
countryNotes.in: The plenary runs 19:30 to 22:30 in Bengaluru; offer the recording and a local follow-up the next day. Diwali (around 8 November 2026, verify) falls in the last week of Mobilize, so set baseline deadlines before it.
countryNotes.tw: The plenary is at 22:00 Taipei, so Taiwan joins the APAC session the next morning. Flag items that touch hours, leave or discipline, because they will need work rules filing and, for hours flexibilities, labor-management meeting approval.
countryNotes.cn: China joins the APAC session. Brief the union contact or employee representatives that rule changes will go through democratic procedure, and name who will keep minutes, sign-in sheets and acknowledgment records.
countryNotes.vn: Vietnam joins the APAC session at 08:00 Hanoi time. Brief the grassroots union chair that changes to internal labor regulations will need consultation and registration, and plan Vietnamese summaries.

templates.name: Current-state baseline assessment
templates.purpose: Rates the current state of each of the 438 Atlas items during Mobilize: whether a document exists, where it lives, how current it is, who owns it, what the gaps are, how risky they are and which wave should fix them. The completed records give every item an owner, a rating and a proposed wave for the Mobilize gate on 6 November 2026 (M04) and feed plan v1.0, the Master checklist and the RAID log.
templates.audience: Item owners and workstream leads (complete the record); country HR leads (jurisdiction details and local adoption evidence); Employment counsel (checks every High rating); PMO (prefills, consolidates and balances waves); steering committee (approves the wave allocation at M04).
templates.when: Mobilize: prefilled by 16 October 2026; completed by owners 19 October to 30 October; workstream calibration 2 to 4 November; PMO consolidation 5 November; Mobilize gate 6 November 2026 (M04). Reused for items added later by change request.
templates.owner: Program management office (CC4), with workstream leads

items.text: Item id
items.detail: Prefilled from the Master checklist: POL-xx for policies, process ids such as ER-02 or PY-01, R-xxx for register obligations.

items.text: Item name
items.detail: Prefilled. Do not rename here; propose a rename in the gaps section.

items.text: Item type
items.detail: Prefilled: Policy / Process / Program / Notice / Filing / Training / Control / Committee / Record.

items.text: Tier
items.detail: Prefilled: Legally required / Public-company driven / Semiconductor-specific / Best practice. The owner confirms or challenges with a reason; Employment counsel decides challenges to a legal tier.

items.text: Workstream
items.detail: WS1 Governance, Ethics and ER / WS2 Talent Acquisition / WS3 HR Operations and Lifecycle / WS4 Total Rewards and Payroll / WS5 Talent, Leave and Engagement / WS6 HR Data, Safety and Systems.

items.text: Jurisdictions in scope
items.detail: Tick all that apply: us, us-ca, us-co, us-nc, us-tx, us-wa, ca, de, il, in, tw, cn, vn. For a global item, complete the jurisdiction rows in the local adoption field for each country where local adoption is needed.

items.text: Assessor role and date assessed
Does a current document exist?
items.detail: Yes, current and approved / Yes, but outdated or never formally approved / Partial: covers some jurisdictions or steps only / No document, but a consistent practice exists / No document and no consistent practice / Not applicable (give the reason, for example below threshold headcount).

items.text: Where does it live?
items.detail: Darwinbox / intranet or SharePoint / Confluence / LMS / shared drive / email or personal files / local country file / vendor portal / other. Paste the link; if it cannot be shared, say who holds it.

items.text: Version and last approval date
items.detail: Version number if any; date of the last formal approval and the approver's role. 'Unknown' is a valid answer and counts as a gap.

items.text: Last reviewed against current law
items.detail: Date and by whom (role). Older than 12 months for a legally required item, or older than the last relevant law change in the country file, is a gap.

items.text: Languages available
items.detail: English / German / Hebrew / Arabic / Traditional Chinese / Simplified Chinese / Vietnamese / French / Spanish / Kannada / Telugu / other. Note which version prevails.

items.text: Local adoption evidence
items.detail: Per jurisdiction where required: signed works agreement (de) / democratic procedure minutes and signed acknowledgments (cn) / filed and approved work rules with approval letter (tw) / registered internal labor regulations with receipt (vn) / certified or model standing orders (in) / none / not required.

items.text: Does practice match the document?
items.detail: Consistent / Minor differences / Material differences (describe) / Unknown. Material differences usually mean the process needs a discovery workshop (T-PM-WORKSHOP).

items.text: Evidence that it was communicated and acknowledged
items.detail: Launch email, LMS acknowledgment report, posting photo or screenshot, training record, none.

items.text: Current owner (role)
items.detail: The role that maintains the item today, even informally.

items.text: Proposed business-as-usual owner (role)
items.detail: The role that will own it after handover on 1 October 2027 (M17). Use roles, never names.

items.text: Ownership status
items.detail: Confirmed / Not confirmed / Disputed. Disputed items go to the workstream lead to resolve by 30 October and to the RAID log if still open.

items.text: Approval chain
items.detail: Global policy / Process document / Legal obligation / Public company and semiconductor control. Prefilled from item type; change only with a reason.

items.text: Subject-matter experts and partners
items.detail: Roles and functions to involve in Discover and Review, for example Payroll, Stock Administration, Trade Compliance, Privacy Office, EHS.

items.text: Country HR lead per jurisdiction
items.detail: Role per jurisdiction ticked above.

items.text: Gap types
items.detail: Tick all that apply: no document / outdated for current law / missing country addendum / no owner / not communicated / no acknowledgment / no control or no control evidence / not translated / not locally adopted, filed or registered / practice differs from document / conflicts with another policy or process / below required standard for public-company or customer audit.

items.text: Gap description
items.detail: Two or three sentences in plain language. Link privileged legal analysis rather than copying it here.

items.text: Impact if the gap is exposed (1 to 5)
items.detail: 5 Severe: statutory breach with penalties, rule unenforceable for discipline or dismissal, SOX key control or SEC disclosure gap. 4 Major: likely claim, regulator or audit finding, or affects a whole country. 3 Moderate: inconsistent practice, employee relations or customer audit finding. 2 Minor: outdated text but compliant practice. 1 Negligible: best-practice improvement only.

items.text: Likelihood of exposure in the next 12 months (1 to 5)
items.detail: 5 Almost certain: external deadline, active audit or known incident. 4 Likely. 3 Possible. 2 Unlikely. 1 Rare.

items.text: Risk score and rating
items.detail: Impact x likelihood (1 to 25). High 15 to 25; Medium 8 to 14; Low 1 to 7. Every High needs an Employment counsel check before 4 November.

items.text: External deadline
items.detail: Statutory or business date the item must meet, for example the California SB 294 notice by 1 February, Ontario written policies by 1 March after a 1 January headcount of 25+, the BC pay transparency report by 1 November, the 10-K filing date.

items.text: Audit, regulator or customer interest
items.detail: SOX key control / SEC or Nasdaq requirement / external auditor request / RBA or customer audit / regulator inquiry / prior internal audit finding / none.

items.text: Effort estimate
items.detail: S up to 5 person-days / M 6 to 15 / L 16 to 30 / XL over 30 (split the item or plan it across two waves).

items.text: Country gates needed
items.detail: Per jurisdiction: consultation body, filing or registration, translation, and realistic lead time in weeks. Use the country gate list on the Countries page; mark (verify) where unconfirmed.

items.text: Proposed wave
items.detail: W1 / W2 / W3 / W4. Rules: required items (legal, public-company or semiconductor tier) rated High, or with an external deadline before 31 March 2027, go to W1, policies before the programs, notices and controls that depend on them; Medium required items to W2; Low required items to W3; best-practice items to W4. Target split of each workstream's required items: about 40% W1, 35% W2, 25% W3.

items.text: Rationale for the proposed wave
items.detail: One sentence, for example 'High risk; unenforceable in China without democratic procedure; must precede ER-04 discipline process'.

items.text: Dependencies
items.detail: Item ids that must be done first or in the same wave.

items.text: Earliest feasible local go-live
items.detail: Allow for the 10-week stage cycle plus country gate lead times and the freeze windows (21 December to 1 January; 5 to 14 February for China, Taiwan and Vietnam).

items.text: RAID entry needed
items.detail: Yes: risk or issue id / No. Required for every High that cannot start in W1.

items.text: Workstream lead decision
items.detail: Agree / Change wave to [W] with reason / Escalate to PMO. Recorded during calibration, 2 to 4 November.

items.text: Employment counsel check (High items only)
items.detail: Agree rating / Change rating to [x] / Needs local counsel. Role and date.

items.text: Rate what exists today, not what should exist. A practice that runs consistently without a document is 'No document, but a consistent practice exists', not a pass.

A document is not locally effective just because it exists. In China, Taiwan, Vietnam, India and Germany, missing adoption evidence is itself a gap rated at least 4 for impact where the rule is used for discipline, hours or pay.
PMO checks before consolidation: every item has an owner status, a risk rating, a proposed wave and a rationale; no High is missing a counsel check; no item is marked Not applicable without a reason.
PMO balances waves against capacity and the 40/35/25 target, records moves with reasons, and presents the allocation at the Mobilize gate on 6 November 2026 (M04).

notes: Prefill everything the catalog already knows (id, name, type, tier, workstream, jurisdictions, default chain) so owners spend their 20 to 30 minutes per item on judgment, not data entry.
Spread the load: 438 items across about 40 owners is roughly 11 each. Owners with more than 20 items get a PMO analyst to pair with them.
Calibrate before consolidating. Each workstream lead runs a 60-minute session to compare scores across owners; uncalibrated ratings make Wave 1 a list of the most anxious owners' items.
The proposed wave is a proposal. The PMO balances capacity and dependencies, and the steering committee approves the allocation at M04; after that, moves need a change request.
Do not paste legal advice or personal data into the baseline. Link privileged memos held by Legal and describe gaps at the level of the rule, not individual cases.
Treat 'Unknown' as a finding. Unknown version, owner or approval date is the most common gap and should be rated, not left blank.
The baseline is reused: Wave 2 to 4 owners update their records at the start of Discover, and items added by change request get a new record.

countryNotes.us: Record the status of federal postings (EEOC Know Your Rights, FLSA, FMLA, USERRA, EPPA, OSHA) and electronic access for remote staff. Rate conduct, confidentiality and social media rules for NLRA Section 7 (Stericycle) and Rule 21F-17 risk, and mark SOX key controls.
countryNotes.us-ca: Check whether EEO and harassment policies are translated into any language spoken by 10%+ of a facility (2 CCR 11023), and whether the pay scale procedure (LC 432.3) and SB 294 notice exist. Items with a 1 February deadline belong in Wave 1.
countryNotes.us-co: Check HFWA notices in English and any language spoken by 5%+ of the workforce, pay range and promotion-notice procedures (C.R.S. 8-5-201) and POWR Act wording; each defective posting is a separate violation, which raises likelihood.
countryNotes.us-nc: Confirm that written wage, PTO forfeiture and bonus rules were given to employees in advance (G.S. 95-25.12, 95-25.13). A forfeiture rule with no proof of advance notice is a gap.
countryNotes.us-tx: Few state-specific items. Check workers' compensation coverage notices in English and Spanish (28 TAC 110.101) and that the harassment policy reflects liability for employers of 1+ and individual supervisors (Labor Code 21.141-21.142).
countryNotes.us-wa: Check pay ranges and benefits descriptions in postings (RCW 49.58.110), PFML notices, the I-9 inspection notice duty from 1 October 2026 and the mini-WARN procedure. Washington changes often mid-year, so record the law date each item reflects.
countryNotes.ca: Rate Ontario and BC separately. Record the 1 January headcount that triggers Ontario's 25+ duties (disconnecting, electronic monitoring, job postings) and BC's 50+ pay transparency report due 1 November; flag any Quebec-based staff.
countryNotes.de: For each item, record whether a works agreement exists or is needed (§87 BetrVG), whether a German version exists and whether statutory postings are current. An English-only rule on a co-determined matter is rated not locally adopted.
countryNotes.il: Record Hebrew versions (and Arabic where employees need them), the sexual-harassment bylaw and its posting, and whether any collective agreement or extension order applies to the item (verify).
countryNotes.in: Record whether standing orders are certified or model standing orders adopted (300+ workers), the status of the Karnataka IT exemption (verify), the GRC and POSH Internal Committee, and bilingual display in English and Kannada or Telugu.
countryNotes.tw: Record whether the item is covered by work rules filed with the local labor authority (the Science Park Bureau for Hsinchu Science Park sites), the approval date and letter number, and whether hours flexibilities rely on labor-management meeting resolutions.
countryNotes.cn: For each rule-type item, record democratic procedure evidence: discussion with the employee congress or all employees, consultation with the union or employee representatives, publication and signed acknowledgments. No evidence means it cannot support an Art. 39 dismissal.
countryNotes.vn: Record whether the item is in the registered internal labor regulations, the registration receipt date, union consultation and the Vietnamese version. Discipline based on rules outside the registered regulations is void.

templates.name: Process discovery workshop guide
templates.purpose: A 90-minute facilitated workshop that captures how a process really runs today: trigger and outcome, swimlanes and hand-offs, decisions, controls and evidence, systems, exceptions and country variations. It gives the Draft stage a validated as-is map to work from, instead of an idealized version written from an old procedure.
templates.audience: Facilitator (trained workstream analyst or HRBP who does not own the process); scribe; process owner; 4 to 8 practitioners who do the work; one country HR representative per region; Internal Audit or the SOX PMO when the process contains a key control; partners such as Payroll, IT or Trade Compliance where they hold a lane.
templates.when: Discover stage (weeks 1 and 2 of an item's 10-week cycle), once per process in scope; Wave 1 workshops start 9 November 2026 (M05). Re-run for a process when its baseline says practice differs materially from the document.
templates.owner: Workstream lead (accountable for the item); PMO facilitator pool

items.text: Fix the scope in one line: the trigger that starts the process and the output that ends it, and the neighboring processes on either side.
Send the baseline record (T-PM-BASELINE), existing procedure documents and the catalog entry for the process to all participants.
Invite the people who do the work, not only their managers: at least one practitioner per lane and one country HR representative per region.
Ask each participant to bring two recent real cases with names removed, and screenshots of the system screens they use.
items.detail: No personal data, health information or case names on the whiteboard or in the notes.

items.text: Prepare a blank swimlane board with draft lanes (role or system) and the four shapes: start, task, decision, end.
Book 90 minutes for the workshop plus 30 minutes for the facilitator and scribe to tidy the map straight after.
Invite Internal Audit or the SOX PMO when the process touches payroll, equity, financial reporting or a known key control.
Thanks for coming. In the next 90 minutes we're going to map how [process] really works today, including the workarounds, so the documentation matches reality.
There are no wrong answers. If what you do differs from the written procedure, that's exactly what we need to know, and nobody will be blamed for it.
We'll use real recent cases with names removed. Please don't mention individual employees or their circumstances.

Improvement ideas are welcome, but we'll park them on a separate list so we map the current process first. By the end we'll have a draft map, a list of controls and exceptions, and open questions with owners.
What starts this process? Walk me through the last time it started.
items.detail: Probes: Who noticed first? Was it a Darwinbox or Greenhouse event, an email request, a ticket, a calendar date? Is there more than one trigger?

items.text: Where does it end? What does 'done' look like, and who knows it's done?
items.detail: Probes: What record, notification or system status shows completion? Who receives the output?

items.text: What happens just before and just after this process that belongs to someone else?
items.detail: Capture the hand-offs in and out and the neighboring process ids, so lanes and controls are not duplicated.

items.text: How many cases a year, and how long does one take from start to finish?
items.detail: Probes: typical and worst case; volume by country; peak periods such as year-end, the compensation cycle or campus season.

items.text: Take the most recent real case. What happened first, and who did it?
items.detail: Write each step as verb plus object ('Validate offer approvals') in the lane of the role that does it. Probe: 'Is that what always happens, or what happened this time?'

items.text: Then what? Who gets it next, and how do they find out?
items.detail: Probes: email, ticket, Darwinbox workflow, chat message, meeting. What do they need from the previous step that is sometimes missing?

items.text: Where does the work wait, and what is it waiting for?
items.detail: Probes: approvals, documents from the employee, a vendor, a payroll cut-off, a country authority. How long is the typical wait?

items.text: Which systems do you touch at this step, and what do you enter or check?
items.detail: Probes: Darwinbox, Greenhouse, payroll provider, LMS, stock administration platform, benefits portals, spreadsheets. Is anything re-keyed by hand? Who has access?

items.text: Where do spreadsheets, personal trackers or other workarounds come in?
items.detail: Probes: Who owns that spreadsheet? Where is it stored? What happens when that person is on leave?

items.text: Here is what the current procedure says for this step. Which is right: the document or what you just described?
items.detail: Record each difference as 'documented vs actual'. Do not resolve it in the room; it becomes an open question for the process owner.

items.text: Where does work get sent back or redone, and why?
items.detail: Probes: the top three reasons, how often, and who fixes it. Rework points are often where a control is missing.

items.text: Where does someone make a decision or judgment call? What are the options, and who decides?
items.detail: Draw a decision diamond with labeled exits. Probe: are the criteria written down or in someone's head?

items.text: Who approves, and what exactly do they check before approving?
items.detail: Probes: delegation of authority and thresholds; what happens when the approver is away; can the requester approve their own request?

items.text: What stops a mistake getting through, and how would you know if something went wrong?
items.detail: Classify each control as preventive or detective, and manual or automated. Note the frequency and who performs it.

items.text: What evidence is left behind that this step happened correctly? Could you show an auditor in 10 minutes?
items.detail: Probes: system log, signed form, approval record, email, report. Where is it stored and for how long?

items.text: Which legal deadlines or notices apply, and how do you track them?
items.detail: Examples: I-9 Section 2 within 3 business days, final pay timing, statutory notices, works council hearing, union notification. Check against the country files.

items.text: Who sees personal or sensitive data in this process, and should they?
items.detail: Probes: health or family data, compensation, investigations; cross-border transfers to US reviewers (China PIPL, Vietnam PDPL, GDPR).

items.text: What are the most common exceptions, and how are they handled?
items.detail: Probes: executives, Section 16 officers, interns, contingent workers, employees on leave, rehires, employees in a second country.

items.text: Tell me about a case in the last year that went badly. What happened, and what changed afterwards?
items.detail: No names. Look for missing controls, unclear ownership and legal near-misses.

items.text: What is different in your country? Walk me through the steps that change.
items.detail: Ask each country representative in turn. Probes: local approvals, forms and language, timing, authority filings, statutory registers.

items.text: Which steps need a works council, union, employee representative or authority?
items.detail: Probes: Germany §87, §99 and §102 BetrVG; China union notification before unilateral termination; Vietnam union in disciplinary meetings; Taiwan labor-management meeting approvals; India GRC or standing orders.

items.text: If you could change one thing about this process, what would it be?
items.detail: Record on the improvement list, not on the as-is map.

sections.title: Close and capture (1:20 to 1:30) and after

items.text: Here's what I heard: the process starts when [trigger] and ends when [outcome]. It runs through [n] steps across [lanes], with [n] decisions and [n] controls. What did I get wrong or leave out?
Read back the open questions and the documented-versus-actual differences, each with an owner and a due date.
Agree validation: the draft map goes out within 3 business days and participants comment within 5 business days.
Clean the swimlane into standard notation (start, task, decision, end; one verb per task; every decision with labeled exits) and load it to the process record on the Processes page.
Log missing controls, legal gaps and ownership disputes in the RAID log, and link them to the item.
Set the item's Discover stage to done in the Master checklist only when the process owner has confirmed the validated map.
The most common failure is documenting the ideal process instead of the real one. If the map has no exceptions, no waits and no workarounds, it is probably wrong.

notes: Ninety minutes is enough for one process if the scope is fixed beforehand. Split any process with more than about 25 steps or more than six lanes into two workshops.
Invite the people who do the work. Managers tend to describe the process as designed; practitioners describe the process as run.
The facilitator should not own the process. A neutral facilitator can ask 'why' without defending the current design.
Map the as-is first and keep improvements on a separate list. The Draft stage decides which improvements to adopt, with the owner and Legal.
Run by video with a shared whiteboard. For APAC or Israel variations, hold a short follow-up in local working hours rather than asking people to join late at night.
Use real cases with names removed and keep personal data out of the notes and board; the workshop record is a program document, not an HR case file.
Capture controls and evidence in the room. They are what Internal Audit samples at the audit readiness review on 24 September 2027 (M16).

countryNotes.us: Capture federal timing controls (I-9 Section 2 within 3 business days, FMLA notices within 5 business days, COBRA notices) and steps where NLRA Section 7 rights affect conduct or confidentiality handling. Involve the SOX PMO for payroll, equity and disclosure processes.
countryNotes.us-ca: Capture California variations such as final pay timing (Labor Code 201-203), meal and rest rules, paid sick leave, CCPA notice at collection and the harassment training cadence.
countryNotes.us-co: Capture Colorado steps: same-day notice of promotional opportunities, post-selection notices within 30 days, HFWA documentation limits and FAMLI handling.
countryNotes.us-nc: Capture where written advance notice of pay or policy changes is given (G.S. 95-25.13) and how WARN notices reach NC Commerce and local officials.
countryNotes.us-tx: Capture Texas final pay timing (Labor Code 61.014) and the Texas Workforce Commission as the WARN dislocated-worker unit; otherwise the federal flow usually applies.
countryNotes.us-wa: Capture pay ranges in postings, PFML notices within 5 business days, the 21-day personnel file and discharge-reason statement on request (HB 1308), and the I-9 inspection notice steps.
countryNotes.ca: Map Ontario and BC variations separately where they differ: ESA notices, the Ontario 45-day response to interviewed applicants, joint health and safety committees, and BC pay transparency.
countryNotes.de: Mark every step where the works council has rights (§87 co-determination, §99 consent to hires and transfers, §102 hearing before dismissal) and every wet-ink requirement (§623 BGB, fixed-term clauses). Keep workshop records anonymous so they are not used to assess individuals.
countryNotes.il: Capture the pre-dismissal hearing, Hebrew-language documents and notices, reserve-duty protections and Form 101 at hire (verify details against the country file). Hold Israel follow-ups Sunday to Thursday.
countryNotes.in: Capture Karnataka or Telangana state variations, domestic enquiry steps for discipline, full and final settlement within 2 working days under the Labour Codes, and POSH Internal Committee timelines.
countryNotes.tw: Capture steps that need labor-management meeting approval (overtime, flexible hours), references to the filed work rules, Traditional Chinese forms and the LSA Art. 16 notice scale.
countryNotes.cn: Capture union notification before unilateral termination (LCL Art. 43), democratic procedure for rule changes, social insurance and housing fund steps, Chinese-language forms and separate PIPL consent for transfers to US reviewers.
countryNotes.vn: Capture union participation in disciplinary meetings for members, references to the registered internal labor regulations, Vietnamese minutes, provincial authority notices and PDPL handling of cross-border data.

templates.name: Policy review checklist
templates.purpose: The checklist every reviewer uses in the Review stage to test a policy draft for completeness, legal accuracy, consistency, plain language, country addenda, controls, accessibility and a workable effective date. A draft enters its approval chain only when every applicable line is marked Pass or carries a logged exception with an owner and date.
templates.audience: Policy owner (runs the review and resolves comments); workstream lead (consistency); Employment counsel and local counsel (legal lines); regional and country HR leads (addenda and local gates); HR Change and Communications (plain language); accessibility reviewer; Privacy Office where personal data is processed.
templates.when: Review stage (2 weeks) after the draft is submitted. Wave 1 drafts are due 18 December 2026 (M06) and are reviewed 4 to 15 January 2027 so approvals close by 29 January (M07); Wave 2 and 3 drafts are reviewed after M10 (9 April 2027) and M13 (9 July 2027).
templates.owner: Employment counsel (legal lines, CC2); policy owner (overall completion); PMO (checks the record before the approval chain opens)

items.text: The draft uses the standard policy template (T-POLICY) with every section completed or marked 'not applicable' with a reason.
The header shows policy id, title, version, owner role, approver role, tier, effective date, next review date and the jurisdictions covered.
Purpose and scope state who is covered (employees, interns, contingent workers, directors) and who is not.
Defined terms are used consistently and match the library glossary.
Roles and responsibilities are written as roles, and each 'must' has an owner.
Related policies, processes and register obligations are linked by id (for example POL-09, ER-03, R-xxx) and the links work.
A redline against the previous version and a short summary of changes are attached; for a new policy, the summary explains what it replaces.
Each jurisdiction's legal requirements for this topic are mapped to a clause, with the citation from the country file; any '(verify)' point is confirmed by local counsel or logged as an exception.
Every linked legally required register obligation (R-xxx) is met by the policy or by a named process.
Conduct, confidentiality, social media, recording and monitoring rules have been checked against NLRA Section 7 (Stericycle) for the US.
Confidentiality wording keeps the required carve-outs: SEC Rule 21F-17, DTSA immunity notice, California Gov Code 12964.5, Colorado POWR Act and Washington Silenced No More (RCW 49.44.211).
A non-retaliation statement and at least one reporting channel other than the direct manager are included where the topic allows complaints.
Where the policy processes personal data, a privacy notice reference is included for each regime that applies (GDPR, PIPL, DPDP, Vietnam PDPL, Israel privacy law, CCPA, BC PIPA).

Public-company requirements are met where relevant: consistency with SEC filings (for example insider trading policy as 10-K Exhibit 19, clawback policy as Exhibit 97), Nasdaq rules and disclosure controls.
Export-control, data security and semiconductor-specific obligations that interact with this topic are referenced (for example deemed-export screening for hiring or access policies).
No conflict with the Code of Business Conduct (POL-01) or any other live policy; overlapping rules are cross-referenced rather than repeated.
The steps the policy describes match the documented process (same roles, approvals, thresholds and timelines).
Approval thresholds match the delegation of authority, and HR systems (Darwinbox, Greenhouse, payroll, LMS) can support what the policy requires.

No conflict with existing works agreements, collective agreements, filed work rules, registered internal labor regulations or standing orders; where there is a conflict, the change route is identified.
Terms that affect pay, leave or benefits match plan documents, payroll configuration and offer letter templates.
Most sentences are under 25 words, in active voice, and the text reads at about a grade 9 to 10 level.
'Must' is used for requirements and 'may' for permissions, consistently; 'should' is used only for guidance.
The hardest rules have a short example, and headings tell the reader what the section answers.
Procedural detail that changes often (forms, system steps, contacts) is moved to the process or a guideline, so the policy stays stable.
After plain-language edits, Employment counsel has re-checked that legal meaning did not change.
For each of the 13 jurisdictions, there is either a country addendum or a recorded decision that none is needed.
Each addendum says that it prevails over the global text where it gives more rights or where local law requires.

Local language versions needed are listed (for example German, Hebrew, Traditional and Simplified Chinese, Vietnamese, French for Quebec, California 10%+ languages, Kannada or Telugu displays) with the prevailing language stated.

Every local gate is flagged with lead time: works council (de), democratic procedure (cn), internal labor regulation consultation and registration (vn), work rules filing and labor-management meeting (tw), standing orders (in), union or representative consultation (il, where applicable).
Local effective dates are set for jurisdictions where gates make them later than the global date.
Local counsel sign-off is recorded where the country file or Employment counsel requires it.
A bilingual reviewer has checked one translated version against the source for legal terms before all translations are ordered.
Controls are defined for the key requirements: who checks what, how often, and what evidence is kept.
Acknowledgment and training needs are stated (who, by when, which LMS assignment) and match the mandatory training matrix (POL-45).
Records created under the policy have retention periods consistent with HR Records Retention (POL-49).
The published version meets WCAG 2.1 AA: real headings, alt text for images and diagrams, sufficient contrast, simple tables and tagged PDFs.
Employees without regular computer access can get the policy (printed copy, posting, kiosk or manager briefing), consistent with Accessibility and Inclusion (POL-57).
The effective date allows for every local gate, notice period and translation, and does not fall in a freeze window (21 December to 1 January; 5 to 14 February for China, Taiwan and Vietnam).
Transition rules cover in-flight cases (for example open leave requests, pending investigations or bonus plan years already started).
Launch communications and manager talking points are drafted (T-PM-LAUNCH-COMMS) and the country launch checklists (T-PM-COUNTRY-LAUNCH) are opened.
Documents to be retired on publication are listed, with their locations.
The next review date is no more than 12 months after the effective date, or earlier where law requires.
All review comments in Atlas are resolved or logged as exceptions with an owner and date, and each reviewer has recorded Pass in the item record.

notes: Mark each line Pass, Fix or N/A. A Fix must be resolved, or logged as an exception with owner and date, before the item enters its approval chain; N/A needs a one-line reason.
Review in parallel, not in sequence. Legal, country, plain-language and accessibility reviewers all work in the same 2-week window and comment on the same draft.
Comment in Atlas, not by email, so comments and their resolution form part of the evidence record.
Privileged legal advice goes in a separate memo held by Legal. The checklist records only that the legal review was done and by which role.
Use the country files and the obligations register as the baseline of local requirements. Anything still marked '(verify)' at the end of Review needs local counsel or an exception.
Protect reviewer time in January: Wave 1 drafts arrive on 18 December, the year-end freeze runs to 1 January, and approvals must close by 29 January (M07).

countryNotes.us: Check conduct and confidentiality rules against NLRA Section 7 (Stericycle), keep the Rule 21F-17 and DTSA language, confirm at-will statements are consistent across policies and offer letters, and check references to federal postings.
countryNotes.us-ca: Confirm FEHA protected categories and the complaint-process elements of 2 CCR 11023, translation where 10%+ of a facility speaks another language, the Gov Code 12964.5 carve-out, LC 432.3 pay scale rules and the CCPA notice at collection.
countryNotes.us-co: Confirm the POWR Act confidentiality carve-out (C.R.S. 24-34-407), EPEWA posting and promotion rules, HFWA terms and that HFWA notices are planned in English and any language spoken by 5%+ of the workforce.
countryNotes.us-nc: Confirm that PTO forfeiture and bonus conditions are written and will be given in advance (G.S. 95-25.12, 95-25.13), and that any reduction in pay has at least one full pay period of written notice.
countryNotes.us-tx: Confirm that the harassment policy reflects liability for employers of 1+ and for individual supervisors (Labor Code 21.141-21.142) and that deduction authorizations are in a language the employee understands.
countryNotes.us-wa: Confirm the Silenced No More carve-out (RCW 49.44.211), the captive-audience rule (RCW 49.44.250), noncompete limits including ESHB 1155 from 30 June 2027, and pay transparency wording.
countryNotes.ca: Review Ontario and BC addenda: Ontario disconnecting-from-work and electronic monitoring policy content, the OHSA harassment program (including virtual harassment), AODA, BC PIPA notices, and French versions for any Quebec-based staff (Bill 96).
countryNotes.de: Identify co-determined content (§87(1) BetrVG, for example conduct rules, working time, monitoring tools, pay principles) and send it to the works council before approval. Require a German version, the AGG complaint office, the HinSchG channel and a GDPR Art. 13 notice.
countryNotes.il: Require a Hebrew version, the sexual-harassment bylaw elements, the Amendment 13 privacy notice, and a check of any collective agreement or extension order that covers the topic (verify).
countryNotes.in: Check consistency with certified or model standing orders, POSH Act policy elements and Internal Committee details, DPDP notice, the Labour Codes 'wages' definition where pay is involved, and bilingual display needs.
countryNotes.tw: Require a Traditional Chinese version, flag content that must sit in the filed work rules (LSA Art. 70), note hours flexibilities that need labor-management meeting approval, and check the PDPA and the 2026 workplace bullying measures.
countryNotes.cn: Require a Simplified Chinese version that prevails, flag rules affecting employees' vital interests for democratic procedure (LCL Art. 4), check separate PIPL consent for cross-border transfers, and make disciplinary grounds specific enough to support Art. 39.
countryNotes.vn: Require a Vietnamese version, flag content that must be in the internal labor regulations for union consultation and registration (LC Arts. 118-119), include the sexual harassment section, and confirm there are no fines or pay cuts as discipline.

templates.name: Approval and sign-off record
templates.purpose: The evidence record for an item's approval chain: which version was approved, by whom, in what role, when, under which chain and step, with what conditions, and the outcome of any employee representative consultation or authority filing. It is generated from the Approvals page, completed where Atlas cannot capture a step, and exported as the evidence Internal Audit samples at the audit readiness review on 24 September 2027 (M16).
templates.audience: PMO document control (opens, checks and locks the record); approvers at each chain step; country HR leads (consultation and filing outcome); Employment counsel; Internal Audit and the external auditor (reviewers of evidence).
templates.when: Opened when an item moves from Review to Approve; each step completed within the 2-week Approve stage; consultation and filing fields completed before the local effective date; record locked when the final step closes and the approved version is published.
templates.owner: Program management office document control (CC4); business-as-usual owner after 1 October 2027: HR Policy and Governance (DS-08)

items.text: Item id and name
items.detail: Prefilled from the Master checklist.

items.text: Item type and tier
items.detail: Prefilled: type (Policy, Process, Program, Notice, Filing, Training, Control, Committee, Record) and tier (Legally required, Public-company driven, Semiconductor-specific, Best practice).

items.text: Approval chain
items.detail: Global policy / Process document / Legal obligation / Public company and semiconductor control / Project document. A change of chain after submission needs a PMO note with the reason.

items.text: Version submitted
items.detail: Version label (for example v2.0 RC1), link to the exact file and its document fingerprint (hash) generated by Atlas, so the approved and published versions can be matched.

items.text: Redline and summary of changes
items.detail: Links to the redline against the previous approved version and the change summary.

items.text: Jurisdictions and addenda included
items.detail: List of the 13 jurisdiction ids covered, with the addenda and language versions attached to this submission.

items.text: Review stage record
items.detail: Link to the completed policy review checklist (T-PM-POLICY-REVIEW) or process validation; list open exceptions with owner and date.

items.text: Submitted by (role) and date
items.detail: Normally the item owner. Submission date starts the 2-week Approve stage clock.

sections.title: Step log
sections.intro: One block per step. Atlas fills most fields automatically; the PMO completes any manual fields.

items.text: Step id and name
items.detail: Prefilled from the chain, for example policy s3 'Legal review'.

items.text: Approver role and approver
items.detail: Role from the chain plus the named approver configured at M03. Names live in Atlas user records, not in this template.

items.text: Delegate and delegation reference
items.detail: Only where a delegate acts: delegation document or Atlas delegation entry, with its start and end dates.

items.text: Decision
items.detail: Approved / Approved with conditions / Sent back (reason required) / Recused (conflict of interest, delegate named) / Skipped (optional steps only, reason required).

items.text: Date and time (UTC) and method
items.detail: Atlas e-approval / email approval attached by the PMO with full headers within 2 business days / wet-ink signature where local law requires it (scan attached).

items.text: Conditions and comments
items.detail: Conditions must be specific, with owner and due date. Do not record legal advice here; reference the privileged memo held by Legal.

items.text: Rule 'all' steps: decision per region
items.detail: For policy s4 (Regional HR review), one decision each from Americas, EMEA and APAC; the step completes only when all three approve.

items.text: Conflict of interest declared
items.detail: Yes / No. An approver who drafted the item or is personally affected recuses and a delegate approves.

sections.title: What each approver confirms
sections.intro: Approvers confirm these points by approving. The chain definitions come from project-core and are configured on the Approvals page.

items.text: Global policy s1, Owner sign-off (Policy owner): the draft is complete, uses the standard template and includes every country addendum.
Global policy s2, Workstream review (Workstream lead): consistent with related policies and processes.
Global policy s3, Legal review (Employment counsel): legal requirements met in every jurisdiction; local counsel engaged where needed.
Global policy s4, Regional HR review (Regional HR leads, all): addenda are workable and consultation or filing needs are flagged.
Global policy s5, Employee representative consultation (Country HR lead, optional): outcome recorded in the consultation section, or step skipped with a note where not needed.
Global policy s6, Final approval (Chief People Officer): approves publication and the global and local effective dates.

Process document s1 to s4: process owner confirms the flow matches how work is done, including exceptions; workstream lead checks hand-offs and the governing policy; Internal Audit or the SOX PMO reviews key or SOX-relevant controls (optional otherwise); Head of HR Operations approves publication and confirms systems and training are ready.

Legal obligation s1 to s3: item owner confirms the obligation is met and evidence is filed; Employment counsel or Compliance confirms the evidence satisfies the requirement and the next due date is set; country HR lead confirms local completion, language and posting or filing.

Public company and semiconductor control s1 to s3: control owner confirms design and evidence; SOX PMO or Trade Compliance confirms the control is designed effectively and testable; General Counsel or delegate approves for audit and disclosure purposes.

Project document s1 to s3: HR Program Manager confirms completeness and consistency with the plan; any steering committee member records the committee's decision; Chief People Officer gives final approval.

sections.title: Employee representative consultation and filings
sections.intro: Completed by the country HR lead for policy step s5, and for any other item that needs consultation or a filing before it takes effect locally.

items.text: Consultation required?
items.detail: Yes / No, with reason (for example 'no works council at this site', 'not a co-determined matter', 'not a rule affecting vital interests') / Not yet determined. Employment counsel confirms 'No' for de, cn, vn and tw.

items.text: Jurisdiction and body
items.detail: Works council (de) / employee congress or all employees, plus the union or employee representatives (cn) / grassroots trade union (vn) / labor-management meeting (tw) / GRC, works committee or union (in) / representative union under a collective agreement (il, where one exists) / joint health and safety committee (ca, safety items) / other.

items.text: Legal basis
items.detail: For example §87(1) no. 1 or no. 6 BetrVG; LCL Art. 4; LC 2019 Arts. 118-119; LSA Art. 70 and Art. 83; IR Code standing orders; Collective Agreements Law 1957. Mark '(verify)' if unconfirmed.

items.text: Information provided
items.detail: Date, documents and language version given to the body.

items.text: Meetings held
items.detail: Dates, attendee roles, minutes reference; for China include the sign-in sheet; for Vietnam the union's written opinion.

items.text: Outcome
items.detail: Agreed / Agreed with changes / Opinion recorded (no agreement required) / Objection: escalated / Conciliation board (Einigungsstelle) or arbitration / Pending.

items.text: Changes made as a result
items.detail: Link to the redline; if the changes are substantive, the chain restarts from the affected step.

items.text: Filing or registration
items.detail: Authority, date submitted, receipt or approval number, approval date. Taiwan: work rules filed with the local labor authority or Science Park Bureau. Vietnam: internal labor regulations registered with the provincial labor authority within 10 days of issuance, effective 15 days after the authority receives a complete dossier. India: standing orders certification where required.

items.text: Publication and acknowledgment evidence
items.detail: Posting photo or intranet notice, signed or electronic acknowledgment report. Required for China (publicity under democratic procedure) and Vietnam (posting at the workplace).

items.text: Local effective date
items.detail: Cannot be earlier than consultation completion, filing or registration effect, and publication. Atlas blocks a Live status before this date.

items.text: Final decision and effective dates
items.detail: Global effective date and each local effective date that differs.

items.text: Published version and location
items.detail: Version label and fingerprint must match the approved version; link to the Policy guide or Processes page.

items.text: Superseded documents retired
items.detail: List with locations and the date each was archived read-only.

items.text: Retention
items.detail: Kept for the period set in HR Records Retention (POL-49) for policy and approval records; prior versions archived read-only.

items.text: Every mandatory step is complete; every optional step is completed or skipped with a recorded reason.
No approver approved their own draft, and every delegate has a valid delegation reference.
No approval or launch is dated inside a freeze window unless the sponsor approved an exception, and the exception is attached.
The published file matches the approved fingerprint; any later change, other than non-substantive corrections logged by the PMO with the owner's agreement, restarted the chain.
Email approvals and wet-ink scans are attached within 2 business days of the decision.
The record is locked, exported as PDF to the evidence folder named by item id and jurisdiction, and the item is flagged for possible Internal Audit sampling.

notes: The Atlas audit trail is the primary evidence. This template defines what the trail must contain and the export format for audit; do not keep a parallel spreadsheet of approvals.

Approvers approve a specific version. Any substantive change after a step restarts the chain from the earliest affected step; the PMO decides what is non-substantive and logs it with the owner's agreement.
Rule 'all' steps need a decision from each region, not one person speaking for all three.
Optional steps are completed or skipped with a reason. A silent skip of the employee representative consultation step is the finding auditors and local regulators look for first.
Keep consultation minutes in the original language with an English summary, and store filing receipts as issued. The local-language document is what an authority or court will read.
Email approvals are a fallback for approvers who cannot reach Atlas; attach the original message with headers, not a forwarded copy.
Internal Audit samples 40 items at M16. A record that passes the integrity checks at the time of approval avoids a scramble in September 2027.

countryNotes.us: There is no consultation step: mark s5 'Not required: no representative body'. For public-company items, the General Counsel step and SOX evidence standards apply, so keep the record ready for the external auditor's testing.
countryNotes.us-ca: Mark s5 'Not required'. Attach evidence of translated versions where 2 CCR 11023 applies and the distribution and acknowledgment record for EEO and harassment policies.
countryNotes.us-co: Mark s5 'Not required'. Keep training and acknowledgment records linked to POWR Act prevention steps for at least 5 years.
countryNotes.us-nc: Mark s5 'Not required'. Record the date written notice of any pay, PTO or bonus change was given, at least one full pay period before the change took effect (G.S. 95-25.13).
countryNotes.us-tx: Mark s5 'Not required'. Record the languages used for workers' compensation notices where the item covers them (28 TAC 110.101).
countryNotes.us-wa: Mark s5 'Not required' unless a union represents the affected employees. Record that any employee meeting used to launch the item was not mandatory where it touched topics covered by RCW 49.44.250.
countryNotes.ca: Mark s5 'Not required' outside unionized workplaces. For health and safety items, record consultation with the joint health and safety committee (20+ workers) or the health and safety representative, and the Ontario annual review date.
countryNotes.de: Record the works council steps: date information was given, the co-determination right engaged (§87 BetrVG), the signed works agreement or regulation agreement, or the Einigungsstelle decision. The local effective date follows signature, and the works agreement must be made available in the workplace (§77(2)).
countryNotes.il: Record whether a representative union exists for the bargaining unit and whether the item needs negotiation or consultation under a collective agreement (verify). Record the approved Hebrew version.
countryNotes.in: Record standing orders certification or adoption of model standing orders where 300+ workers are employed, any GRC or works committee consultation, Internal Committee notification for POSH items, and bilingual display evidence.
countryNotes.tw: Record the labor-management meeting resolution (date and minutes) where hours flexibilities are involved, the work rules filing date, the authority (local labor bureau or Science Park Bureau), the approval letter number and posting evidence.
countryNotes.cn: Record each democratic procedure step: draft circulated to the employee congress or all employees, comments received, consultation with the union or employee representatives (minutes and sign-in sheets), final text, publication and signed acknowledgments. The Chinese version prevails.
countryNotes.vn: Record union consultation minutes or written opinion, the registration dossier submitted to the provincial labor authority within 10 days of issuance, the receipt date, the effective date 15 days after a complete dossier is received, and workplace posting evidence.

templates.name: Weekly status report
templates.purpose: The weekly one-page report from the PMO to the sponsor, workstream leads and regional HR leads: overall RAG, progress by wave and workstream, approvals pending, overdue items, top risks and issues, decisions needed and next week's plan. Counts are generated from the Master checklist, Approvals and RAID log, and leads add short commentary, so there is one version of the truth that also feeds the steering committee pack.
templates.audience: Chief People Officer (sponsor); workstream leads (WS1 to WS6); cross-cutting leads (CC1 to CC4); regional and country HR leads; steering committee members (read-only); item owners (see their own overdue items).
templates.when: Weekly from 16 October 2026. Owners update the Master checklist by Wednesday close of business local time; PMO data snapshot Thursday 08:00 Pacific; lead commentary by Thursday 14:00 Pacific; published on Project HQ Friday 08:00 Pacific. Short reports only on 25 December 2026 and 1 January 2027 (year-end freeze).

items.text: Report date and week
items.detail: For example 'Friday 22 January 2027; Wave 1, week 11 of 14'.

items.text: Overall RAG
items.detail: Green: next milestone on track. Amber: next milestone at risk, with a recovery plan that keeps it within the current wave. Red: a milestone will be missed without a sponsor or steering committee decision, extra resource or a change request.

items.text: Trend since last week
items.detail: Improving / Stable / Worsening, with one reason.

items.text: Headline
items.detail: Three sentences at most: what moved, what is at risk, what is needed.

items.text: Next milestone and confidence
items.detail: Milestone id, date and the measure, for example 'M06 Wave 1 drafts complete, 18 Dec 2026: 82% of Wave 1 drafts submitted, forecast 95% by the date'.

items.text: Milestones in the next 8 weeks
items.detail: Id, date, status (On track / At risk / Late / Done).

items.text: Items by stage for the current wave

items.text: Wednesday: PMO sends a reminder to owners with stage dates in the next 10 business days.
Thursday 08:00 Pacific: take the data snapshot from the Master checklist, Approvals and RAID log; do not edit counts by hand.
Check each RAG against the definitions; challenge any workstream that stays Green while its overdue count rises.
Confirm that every Red has been discussed with the sponsor before publication. There are no surprise Reds.
Keep the body to one page; detail goes in the appendix generated from Atlas.
Publish on Project HQ at 08:00 Pacific Friday, notify the distribution list, and archive the PDF with the week number.
Use roles and item ids in overdue lists. The report goes to a wide audience and is not a performance tool for individuals.

notes: The report is only as good as the Master checklist. If owners don't update by Wednesday, the counts are wrong; the Wednesday reminder and the stale-record list are how the PMO keeps data current.
RAG is by definition, not by mood. Amber and Red always come with a recovery action and a date, and the PMO can override a workstream's self-assessed RAG with a note.
Watch for 'watermelon' reporting: green on the outside, red inside. Rising overdue counts, long approval waits or stalled country gates under a Green RAG are challenged before publication.
Executives read the headline and the decisions needed. Put the ask in the first five lines.
Use the same snapshot for the steering committee pack (T-PM-STEERCO) so there is never a second set of numbers.
During the freezes (21 December to 1 January, and 5 to 14 February for China, Taiwan and Vietnam), publish a short report focused on what resumes after the freeze.
