templates.name: Steering committee pack and agenda
templates.purpose: The standard pack and 90-minute agenda for the Project Atlas steering committee, built so the committee takes decisions on gates, change requests, red risks and escalations rather than hearing updates. It also sets the gate criteria for each gate milestone and the minimum content of minutes.
templates.audience: Steering committee members as set in the charter (typically the Chief People Officer as chair and sponsor, General Counsel or delegate, the Chief Compliance Officer, a Finance delegate, the HRIS director and the regional HR leads, with Internal Audit as observer); HR Program Manager (secretary); workstream leads and Employment counsel by invitation.
templates.when: Monthly, plus gate meetings at M02 (23 October 2026), M04 (6 November 2026), M07 (29 January 2027), M08 (12 February 2027), M11 (14 May 2027), M14 (13 August 2027), M16 (24 September 2027) and M18 (8 October 2027). No meetings 21 December to 1 January. Pack issued 3 business days before each meeting.
templates.owner: HR Program Manager (CC4), on behalf of the sponsor

items.text: Take the pack data from the latest weekly status snapshot; do not run a separate data collection.

Ask each lead with a decision on the agenda for a one-page decision paper: issue, two or three options, impact on scope, schedule, cost and risk, recommendation, and what happens if no decision is made.
Hold a 30-minute pre-brief with the sponsor to agree the agenda, the decisions sought and any sensitive items.
Mark legal content that is privileged, keep the advice in a counsel memo, and make sure Employment counsel attends when it is discussed.
Issue the pack on Project HQ 3 business days before the meeting and send the link; late papers move to the next meeting unless the chair agrees.
Confirm quorum: the chair or delegate plus at least half of members, including Legal for any decision that accepts legal risk.
One-page summary: overall RAG, milestone confidence, decisions sought.
Milestone tracker M01 to M18: planned date, forecast, status and gate criteria.
Progress by wave and workstream: items by stage, planned versus actual, burn-up.
Country gate tracker for all 13 jurisdictions: consultations, filings and registrations, translations, local effective dates.
Approvals pending over 5 business days and overdue items by workstream.
Red and rising Amber risks with mitigation status, and issues needing escalation.
Change requests for decision, each with its impact assessment (T-PM-CHANGE-REQUEST).
Resourcing and budget: FTE plan versus actual, spend versus budget, vendor usage (translation, local counsel).
Decision log since the last meeting and open actions.
0:00-0:05 Opening: quorum, conflicts of interest, approval of previous minutes, open actions.
0:05-0:15 Program status and milestone confidence; questions on the pack only, no re-presentation.
0:15-0:40 Gate decision (at gate meetings) or deep dive on one wave, workstream or country (at monthly meetings).
items.owner: HR Program Manager and relevant lead

items.text: 0:40-0:55 Change requests for decision.
0:55-1:10 Red risks and escalations, including stalled consultations or filings.
1:10-1:20 Legal and regulatory changes affecting scope (new laws, rescissions, court decisions).
1:20-1:25 Resourcing and budget.
1:25-1:30 Recap of decisions and actions, and the key messages members cascade to their teams.
M02 Charter approved (23 October 2026): scope, resourcing, budget and governance agreed; workstream leads and deputies named; country gate lead times included.
M04 Mobilize gate (6 November 2026): all 438 items have an owner, a current-state rating and a wave; plan v1.0 baselined; approval chains configured and tested (M03).
M07 Wave 1 approvals complete (29 January 2027): every Wave 1 approval chain closed; works council and other consultations started where required.
M08 Wave 1 live (12 February 2027): Wave 1 published, communicated and evidenced in every jurisdiction or with an approved local date; wave retrospective held.
M11 Wave 2 live (14 May 2027) and M14 all required items live (13 August 2027): every legal, public-company and semiconductor item is live with evidence, or covered by an approved change request.
M16 Audit readiness review (24 September 2027): Internal Audit has sampled 40 items and confirmed evidence is complete, or the remediation plan is agreed.
M18 Project close (8 October 2027): close-out report and lessons learned approved; handover to business as usual complete (M17).

Gate decision options: Go / Go with conditions (each with owner and date) / Hold (named gap to close, new decision date) / Re-plan (change request required). Record the option and reasons in the minutes.
Which required items are we least confident will be live with evidence by 13 August 2027, and what would it take to change that?
Where are we waiting on an authority or employee representative body, and what is our fallback if that takes longer than planned?
Are any of the reported Greens hiding long approval waits, stale records or overdue reviews?
What legal risk are we accepting by deferring this item, who accepted it and is that documented?
Are owners and approvers getting the time they were promised, and which leader needs to hear from the sponsor?
Will each item have a business-as-usual owner and review date by 1 October 2027?
Attendees and quorum
items.detail: Roles present, apologies, delegates; whether quorum was met.

items.text: Decisions
items.detail: Each with a RAID decision id, the option chosen, conditions, and who decided. Decisions on the charter, plan and change requests are also recorded as step s2 of the project approval chain.

items.text: Gate outcome
items.detail: Go / Go with conditions / Hold / Re-plan, with conditions, owners and dates.

items.text: Change request decisions
items.detail: CR id and outcome; conditions.

items.text: Actions
items.detail: Owner role, due date; reviewed at the next meeting.

items.text: Messages to cascade
items.detail: Two or three sentences members share with their teams; HR Change and Communications adds them to the communications calendar.

items.text: Circulate draft minutes within 2 business days; the chair approves them, and they are filed on Project HQ.

notes: Decide, don't narrate. Issue the pack 3 business days ahead, assume it has been read, and spend at least 50 of the 90 minutes on decisions.
Every decision paper fits on one page and shows the option of doing nothing. If there is no decision, it belongs in the status report, not the agenda.
Gate meetings use the milestone criteria in project-core. 'Go with conditions' is acceptable only when each condition has an owner and a date that comes back to the committee.
Deferring a legally required item is a risk acceptance, not a scheduling choice. Employment counsel states the exposure in writing and the committee minutes who accepted it.
Plan around the calendar: no meeting during the year-end freeze, and the M08 gate on 12 February 2027 falls inside the Lunar New Year freeze, so APAC gives a written update by 4 February.
Use the same numbers as the weekly status report. A second set of numbers in the pack destroys trust in both.

countryNotes.us: Report public-company items (SOX controls, SEC disclosures, Nasdaq rules, insider trading, clawback) as their own line, given General Counsel and Audit Committee interest, and flag anything that affects the 10-K or proxy timetable.
countryNotes.us-ca: Report California items with fixed dates (SB 294 notice by 1 February, pay data report in May) and items with high litigation exposure, such as wage and hour items with PAGA risk, as gate considerations.
countryNotes.us-co: Report Colorado pay transparency and POWR Act items separately while open, because penalties apply per posting or violation.
countryNotes.us-nc: Escalate North Carolina only when a pay, PTO or bonus change risks breaching the advance written notice rule; otherwise include it in the US roll-up.
countryNotes.us-tx: Include Texas in the US roll-up; there is no state-level gate to report.
countryNotes.us-wa: Report Washington pay-posting exposure (class actions since Branson, 2025) and mid-year law changes as standing risks until the relevant items are live.
countryNotes.ca: Report Ontario and BC readiness separately, and bring any decision on French versions for Quebec-based staff (Bill 96) to the committee.
countryNotes.de: Report the works council status of each German item. The committee decides escalations when negotiations stall, including accepting a later local effective date or going to the Einigungsstelle.
countryNotes.il: Report Hebrew versions and any union or collective agreement constraints (verify), and the effect of reserve duty and holidays on capacity.
countryNotes.in: Report standing-order status and changes to state rules under the Labour Codes (Karnataka, Telangana) as legal-change risks.
countryNotes.tw: Report work rules filing and approval status. The committee accepts that Taiwan's local effective date follows authority approval and posting.
countryNotes.cn: Report democratic procedure status. The committee must not approve a China effective date before the procedure, publication and acknowledgments are complete.
countryNotes.vn: Report internal labor regulation consultation and registration status. The local effective date is 15 days after the authority receives a complete dossier, so the committee plans Vietnam launches accordingly.

templates.name: Change request form
templates.purpose: Controls changes to Project Atlas scope, schedule, resources or budget once plan v1.0 is baselined at the Mobilize gate on 6 November 2026 (M04). Each request is described, assessed for impact, consulted on and decided at the right level, and the decision is applied to the Plan, Master checklist and RAID log.
templates.audience: Anyone on the program can raise a request; the PMO assesses; workstream leads, Employment counsel, regional HR leads and Finance are consulted; the HR Program Manager, Chief People Officer or steering committee decides, according to the thresholds below.
templates.when: Any time after 6 November 2026 that a change is proposed to baselined scope, wave allocation, milestone dates, resourcing, budget or approach, including when a new law, audit finding or business change adds, removes or alters an item. PMO assessment within 5 business days (2 if urgent).
templates.owner: Program management office (CC4); decisions follow the project approval chain

items.text: Change request id
items.detail: CR-001 onwards, assigned by the PMO.

items.text: Title
items.detail: Short and specific, for example 'Move POL-38 country addenda for de and cn from W1 to W2'.

items.text: Raised by (role) and date
Type of change
items.detail: Scope: add / remove / split / merge items, or change jurisdiction coverage. Schedule: move items between waves, move a milestone, change stage dates. Resource: add, remove or reallocate people, local counsel or translation capacity. Budget. Approach or tooling.

items.text: Description
items.detail: What changes, from what to what, in plain language.

items.text: Reason and trigger
items.detail: New law or legal change / audit or regulator finding / business change (acquisition, new site, reorganization) / dependency slip / capacity / consultation or filing delay / error in the baseline / other.

items.text: Items affected
items.detail: Item ids, workstreams and jurisdictions.

items.text: Decision needed by
items.detail: Date and why, for example 'before the Wave 2 start on 15 February 2027' or 'before the works council meeting on [date]'.

items.text: Scope impact
items.detail: Number of items added, removed or moved, by wave and tier.

items.text: Schedule impact
items.detail: Milestones affected (M-ids), effect on stage dates and the critical path, and country gate lead times.

items.text: Resource impact
items.detail: Person-days by role and workstream; vendor hours (translation, local counsel).

items.text: Budget impact
items.detail: USD estimate; within or outside the approved contingency.

items.text: Legal and compliance risk
items.detail: Exposure if the change is approved and if it is not; required for any change that removes or defers a legally required, public-company or semiconductor item.

items.text: Country impact
items.detail: Jurisdictions affected; whether consultation, filing, registration or translation must be redone.

items.text: Dependencies
items.detail: Other items, other change requests, system changes.

items.text: Options considered
items.detail: At least: do nothing, the proposed change, and one alternative, each with pros and cons.

items.text: PMO recommendation
items.detail: Approve / Approve with conditions / Reject / Defer, with a one-paragraph rationale.

items.text: Workstream lead view
items.detail: Required for every request affecting the workstream's items.

items.text: Employment counsel view
items.detail: Required for removing or deferring any required item, and for scope changes driven by law.

items.text: Regional HR lead view
items.detail: Required for any change to jurisdiction coverage or to local dates.

items.text: Finance view
items.detail: Required for budget changes.

items.text: Internal Audit or SOX PMO view
items.detail: Required for changes to control items or to the audit readiness scope at M16.

items.text: HR Program Manager decides: moves within a wave that do not affect a milestone, swaps of items of similar effort, and changes of up to 5 person-days.
Chief People Officer decides: moving items between waves, a milestone slip of up to 2 weeks that does not move a gate milestone, and budget changes within the approved contingency.

Steering committee decides: any change to a gate milestone (M02, M04, M07, M08, M11, M14, M16, M18), removing a required item or deferring it beyond 13 August 2027 (M14), budget beyond contingency, and adding or removing a jurisdiction.
Urgent changes: the sponsor may approve an interim decision by email; the steering committee ratifies it at its next meeting.
Decision
items.detail: Approved / Approved with conditions / Rejected / Deferred to [date] / Withdrawn.

items.text: Decided by (role) and date
items.detail: For steering committee decisions, the minutes reference and RAID decision id.

items.text: Conditions
items.detail: Each with an owner role and date.

items.text: Rationale
items.detail: One or two sentences, including any accepted legal risk and who accepted it.

items.text: Approval chain record
items.detail: Link to the project chain record (PMO review, steering committee, sponsor approval) where the change alters the charter or plan baseline.

items.text: Update the Plan and re-baseline with a new plan version number (v1.1, v1.2 and so on) where dates move.
Update the Master checklist: wave, owner, target stage dates and scope notes for every affected item.
Update the RAID log: close or add risks, record the decision, and link the change request.
Adjust approval chains, country launch checklists and the communications calendar if affected.
Tell affected owners, approvers and regional HR leads within 2 business days of the decision.
Show the change in the next weekly status report and close the request once all updates are done.

notes: Baseline first. Before plan v1.0 is approved at M04, changes are made directly; after 6 November 2026, any change to wave, milestone, scope, resources or budget needs a change request.
Keep decisions at the lowest level that can make them. The thresholds exist so that most requests are decided within a week without waiting for the steering committee.
Removing or deferring a legally required item is a decision to accept risk. Employment counsel describes the exposure in writing, and the steering committee minutes who accepted it.
A new law that adds an obligation is a change request, not an issue. Legal changes flagged in the library's research watchlist should arrive here with the item ids they affect.
Batch small requests for the monthly steering committee; use the urgent route only when waiting would cause a missed legal deadline or a gate failure.
Keep the change log on Project HQ. The count of requests raised, approved and open is part of the weekly status report and the close-out report.

countryNotes.us: Federal rule changes and rescissions (for example EEO-1 reporting, verify current status) and new SEC or Nasdaq requirements arrive as change requests; assess public-company items with the General Counsel's delegate.
countryNotes.us-ca: California laws usually take effect on 1 January; raise change requests for new California requirements by October so items can be updated before the effective date.
countryNotes.us-co: Colorado bills without a safety clause take effect about 90 days after the session ends (12 August in 2026; verify for 2027). Raise the request when the bill is signed, not when it takes effect.
countryNotes.us-nc: Any change that moves the effective date of a pay, PTO or bonus rule must still allow at least one full pay period of written advance notice (G.S. 95-25.13).
countryNotes.us-tx: The Texas legislature meets in odd years, and the 2027 regular session runs from January to late May; new laws commonly take effect on 1 September (verify), so expect any resulting requests in Wave 3.
countryNotes.us-wa: Washington session laws usually take effect in June or July; plan for requests to adjust Wave 3 items after the 2027 session.
countryNotes.ca: Ontario's Working for Workers acts and BC changes arrive regularly; raise a scope request if Quebec headcount appears, because French-language requirements and OQLF registration at 25+ employees would then apply.
countryNotes.de: A change to a co-determined item after the works council has agreed it reopens consultation; include the additional works council lead time in the schedule impact.
countryNotes.il: Assess schedule impacts against Israeli holidays and reserve-duty absences, and include Hebrew re-translation effort in the resource impact.
countryNotes.in: State rules under the four Labour Codes (Karnataka, Telangana) are still being notified; expect requests when rules or the Karnataka IT exemption status change (verify).
countryNotes.tw: A change after the work rules have been filed requires refiling the amended rules and waiting for authority approval; include that time in the schedule impact.
countryNotes.cn: A change to a rule after democratic procedure means repeating the procedure for the changed provisions, then publishing again and collecting acknowledgments; include that lead time.
countryNotes.vn: A change after registration means consulting the union again and re-registering the internal labor regulations, which take effect 15 days after the authority receives a complete dossier.

templates.name: Country launch checklist
templates.purpose: Takes an approved policy, process or obligation live in one jurisdiction: local plan, employee representative consultation, translation, filing or registration, posting, acknowledgment, local manager briefing and evidence. An item is Live in a jurisdiction only when every applicable line here is done or marked not applicable with a reason.
templates.audience: Country HR leads (complete one checklist per item per jurisdiction); regional HR leads (assure); Employment counsel and local counsel; HR Change and Communications; LMS administrators; PMO (checks evidence before setting the item to Live).
templates.when: Opened when an item enters Review (long-lead gates such as works council consultation, democratic procedure, work rules filing and internal labor regulation registration start then); completed in the Go live week. Wave live milestones: 12 February 2027 (M08), 14 May 2027 (M11), 13 August 2027 (M14).
templates.owner: Country implementation (CC1), led by the regional HR leads

items.text: Confirm the local scope: which entity, sites and employee groups are covered, and whether the item applies at the local headcount (for example Ontario 25+, Taiwan work rules 30+, Vietnam internal labor regulations 10+, India standing orders 300+).
Confirm the country addendum and the global text approved in the approval record (T-PM-APPROVAL-RECORD).
Decide whether the change is less favorable to employees in any respect; if so, get Employment counsel's view on consent, notice or consultation before going further.
List the local gates that apply (consultation, filing or registration, translation, posting) with their lead times, and record them on the Countries page.

Work back from the target date to set the local effective date, allowing for each gate, notice periods, freeze windows (21 December to 1 January; 5 to 14 February for China, Taiwan and Vietnam) and local holidays.
Set up the LMS assignment rule for the jurisdiction (population, language version, due date) and test it with one record.
Confirm who in the country signs off each line of this checklist and who holds the evidence.

Germany: inform the works council early; where a §87 BetrVG right applies, negotiate and sign a works agreement (or obtain an Einigungsstelle decision) before the item takes effect; observe the §99 or §102 process where hires, transfers or dismissals are involved.

China: run democratic procedure for rules affecting employees' vital interests: discussion by the employee congress or all employees, consultation with the union or employee representatives, final text, then publication with signed acknowledgments.
Vietnam: consult the grassroots union (where one exists) on content that belongs in the internal labor regulations, salary scales, bonus rules or performance criteria, and keep its written opinion.
Taiwan: obtain a labor-management meeting resolution where the item changes overtime, flexible hours or other LSA flexibilities, and keep the minutes.
India: consult the Grievance Redressal Committee or works committee where the item affects their remit, and notify the POSH Internal Committee for harassment items.
Israel: confirm whether a representative union or collective agreement covers the affected employees and, if so, complete any required negotiation or consultation (verify).
Canada: for health and safety items, consult the joint health and safety committee (20+ workers) or the health and safety representative.
Record the outcome, meeting dates and minutes in the consultation section of the approval record before setting a local effective date.
Order translations only after the source text is legally approved, using the program glossary and an approved vendor.

Produce the required versions: German (de), Hebrew and Arabic where employees need it (il), Traditional Chinese (tw), Simplified Chinese (cn), Vietnamese (vn), French for any Quebec-based staff (ca), California languages spoken by 10%+ of a facility for EEO and harassment policies (us-ca), English plus Kannada or Telugu for Indian statutory displays (in).
Have a bilingual HR reviewer and, for legal terms, local counsel check the translation against the source.
State which language version prevails, consistent with local law (for example Chinese in China, Vietnamese in Vietnam).
Load each language version to the Policy guide and LMS with the same version number as the source.
Taiwan: file amended work rules with the local labor authority (the Science Park Bureau for Hsinchu Science Park sites), record the approval letter number and post the approved rules.

Vietnam: register the internal labor regulations with the provincial labor authority within 10 days of issuance; the regulations take effect 15 days after the authority receives a complete dossier; branches in other provinces send the registered regulations to their local authority.

India: certify standing orders or adopt the model standing orders where 300+ workers are employed (verify the Karnataka IT exemption status), and display statutory abstracts in English and the local language.
Germany: make works agreements available in the workplace or on the intranet (§77(2) BetrVG) and update statutory postings (ArbZG, AGG, MuSchG) in German.
US federal and state: update required posters and electronic postings for remote employees, including state notices for each state where staff work.

Ontario: give employees a copy of new or changed written policies required under the ESA (disconnecting from work, electronic monitoring) within 30 days (verify), and post OHSA policies where required.
China and Vietnam: post the published rules at the workplace and on the intranet, and keep dated photos or screenshots as evidence.
Publish the local version on the Policy guide or Processes page and archive the superseded local documents read-only.
Send the launch email (T-PM-LAUNCH-COMMS) in the local language, in local working hours, not on a public holiday or a Friday afternoon.
Brief local managers 2 business days before the employee email, in the local language where needed, using the manager talking points.
Assign the acknowledgment in the LMS; target 98% within 30 days, with escalation to managers at 30 days and to the regional HR lead at 45 days.
Collect signed acknowledgments where local law or practice needs them (China, Vietnam), using e-signature where acceptable and wet ink where not.
Give employees without regular computer access a printed copy or briefing and record it.
Hold an HRBP drop-in or Q&A within 2 weeks and feed new questions into the FAQ.

File the evidence pack in the evidence folder named by item id and jurisdiction: approval record, consultation minutes, filing receipts, translations, posting photos or screenshots, briefing attendance and acknowledgment report.
Regional HR lead reviews the evidence pack and confirms it is complete.
Set the item to Live for this jurisdiction in the Master checklist, with the local effective date.
Log any open point (for example acknowledgment below target, authority approval pending) in the RAID log with owner and date.
Set the local review date and name the local business-as-usual owner in the item record.

notes: Start long-lead gates during Review, not after approval. Works council negotiations, democratic procedure, work rules filing and internal labor regulation registration can each take longer than the 1-week Go live stage.
Approval is global; going live is local. Atlas shows an item as Live in a jurisdiction only when this checklist is complete there, and the master status rolls up from the 13 jurisdictions.
Never announce a local effective date before the local gates are complete. In China, Taiwan and Vietnam a rule that skipped its gate cannot support discipline.

Wave 1 goes live on 12 February 2027, inside the Lunar New Year and Tet freeze. Plan China, Taiwan and Vietnam Wave 1 launches to complete by 4 February 2027 or to start on 15 February with an approved local date.
Translate once, from the approved source. Translating drafts that later change is the most common cause of rework and mismatched versions.
Evidence is the deliverable. Internal Audit samples 40 items at M16, and a missing receipt or minutes file counts as not done.

countryNotes.us: No consultation is required. Update federal postings (EEOC Know Your Rights, FLSA, FMLA, USERRA, EPPA, OSHA) with electronic access for remote staff, keep rules consistent with NLRA Section 7, and use electronic acknowledgment.
countryNotes.us-ca: Translate EEO and harassment policies into any language spoken by 10%+ of a facility (2 CCR 11023), distribute them with acknowledgment, and give the LC 2810.5 and SB 294 notices in the required languages.
countryNotes.us-co: Give HFWA notices in English and any language spoken by 5%+ of the workforce, update the COMPS and Workplace Public Health Rights posters, and keep acknowledgment records for at least 5 years to support the POWR Act defense.
countryNotes.us-nc: Give written notice of any pay, PTO or bonus change at least one full pay period before it takes effect (G.S. 95-25.13) and keep signed or electronic acknowledgments; Spanish posters are available from NCDOL.
countryNotes.us-tx: Post workers' compensation notices in English, Spanish and any other language common to the workforce (28 TAC 110.101); otherwise follow the US federal steps.
countryNotes.us-wa: Keep manager briefings to policy content: meetings on political, religious or union topics must be voluntary (RCW 49.44.250). Post I-9 inspection notices in English and the five most common other Washington languages from 1 October 2026, and update L&I and ESD posters.
countryNotes.ca: English is fine for Ontario and BC, but Quebec-based staff need French versions (Bill 96). Give Ontario employees copies of required written policies within 30 days (verify), post OHSA documents, and give BC PIPA notices where personal data is involved.
countryNotes.de: Involve the works council early and allow 8 to 12 weeks for consultation and a possible Einigungsstelle (verify for each topic). Publish in German, make works agreements available (§77(2) BetrVG), and do not go live on a co-determined matter before agreement.
countryNotes.il: Provide Hebrew versions (Arabic where employees need them), post the sexual-harassment bylaw summary in Hebrew, and schedule launches Sunday to Thursday outside the Jewish holidays (verify dates).
countryNotes.in: Display statutory abstracts, the POSH policy and Internal Committee details in English and Kannada or Telugu, keep standing orders consistent (verify the Karnataka IT exemption), and avoid launching in Diwali week.
countryNotes.tw: File amended work rules with the local labor authority or the Science Park Bureau and post them, get labor-management meeting resolutions for hours flexibilities, publish a Traditional Chinese version, and avoid 5 to 14 February 2027.
countryNotes.cn: Complete democratic procedure (employee congress or all employees, consultation with the union or representatives), publish with signed acknowledgments, keep minutes and sign-in sheets, make the Simplified Chinese version prevail, and avoid the Lunar New Year freeze.
countryNotes.vn: Consult the grassroots union, register the internal labor regulations within 10 days of issuance (effective 15 days after a complete dossier is received), post them at the workplace, publish a Vietnamese version, and avoid the Tet freeze.

templates.name: Policy launch email and manager talking points
templates.purpose: The standard launch package for an approved policy: the employee email, manager talking points, what managers should not say and the employee FAQ, with [Placeholders] to complete for each policy and country. It makes every launch consistent, plain and legally safe, and it drives the acknowledgment that counts as evidence.
templates.audience: HR Change and Communications lead (prepares and localizes); policy owner and Employment counsel (approve the summary and FAQ answers); people managers (deliver talking points); country HR leads (local versions and timing); all employees in scope (receive the email).
templates.when: Go live stage, after final approval and after local gates are complete. Managers are briefed 2 business days before the employee email; the email goes out on the local effective date or up to 5 business days before it; reminders at day 14 and day 30.
templates.owner: HR Change and Communications (CC3), with the policy owner

items.text: Policy owner and Employment counsel approve the change summary, FAQ answers and any country-specific lines.
Country HR leads confirm local gates are complete and the local effective date, and provide localized versions.
Schedule the send for local working hours on a working day, not a Friday afternoon, a public holiday or a freeze window.
Brief managers 2 business days before the employee email, and share the talking points and FAQ.
Confirm the LMS acknowledgment assignment is live and the link in the email opens the right language version.
Subject: [Policy name]: updated policy effective [effective date]. Please read and acknowledge by [due date].
Hello [all employees in [country or team]],

As part of Project Atlas, our program to document and update every HR policy and process across the company, we have [published a new / updated our] [Policy name]. It takes effect on [effective date] for employees in [jurisdictions].
What is changing: [two to four short points describing the most important changes in plain language]. What is not changing: [the main points that stay the same].
Why we are making this change: [one or two sentences, for example a change in law, making our approach consistent across countries, or making the rules clearer].
What you need to do: read the policy and the addendum for your country, then confirm you have read it in [LMS name] by [due date]. It takes about [x] minutes.
Where to find it: the policy is in the Policy guide at [link], available in [languages]. [Where local law requires: If the language versions differ, the [language] version prevails.]
Questions: talk to your manager, contact your HR business partner at [contact], or use [HR help channel]. Managers will cover the change in team meetings over the next two weeks.

Nothing in this policy limits your right to report possible violations of law to a government agency, to discuss your pay or working conditions where the law protects that, or to raise a concern through [Speak Up channel] without retaliation.
items.detail: Fixed text approved by Legal; keep it in every language version.

items.text: Thank you, [Policy owner role] and [Chief People Officer]

sections.title: Manager talking points
sections.intro: Use in a regular team meeting within two weeks of launch. Keep to the approved summary.

items.text: I want to take five minutes on an HR policy update that affects our team: [Policy name], which takes effect on [date].
It's part of Project Atlas, which is bringing all our HR policies and processes up to date in every country where we work.
The main change for us is [change 1]. In practice that means [example relevant to the team].
The second change is [change 2], so from [date] we will [what employees do differently].
What isn't changing: [main points that stay the same].
Everyone needs to read the policy and confirm it in [LMS name] by [due date]. It takes about [x] minutes.
If you have a question I can't answer today, I'll come back to you by [date], or you can contact [HRBP or HR help channel] directly.
If you're ever worried about how this or any policy is being applied, you can raise it with me, with HR or through [Speak Up channel], and you won't face retaliation for doing so.
What questions do you have?
Don't interpret the policy beyond the approved summary or promise exceptions. Refer individual situations to the HRBP.
Don't describe the change as box-ticking or suggest people can ignore it; that undermines the policy and the acknowledgment.
Don't use the briefing to discuss union membership, political or religious matters, or employees' views on representation. In Washington such meetings must be voluntary (RCW 49.44.250).
Don't track who asked questions or what they asked. Acknowledgment is tracked only through the LMS.

sections.title: Employee FAQ
sections.intro: Answers in detail are the approved text; complete the [Placeholders] for each policy.

items.text: Why is this policy changing now?
items.detail: Approved answer: [reason]. Project Atlas is updating every HR policy and process in waves through October 2027, so you may see other updates too.

items.text: Does this apply to me?
items.detail: It applies to [scope, for example all employees and interns in the listed countries]. [Contingent workers follow [contract or supplier terms].] Check the addendum for your country.

items.text: What changes for me in practice?
items.detail: [Two or three concrete examples written for the employee, for example how to request leave or report a concern under the new policy.]

items.text: Is my country's version different?
items.detail: Your country addendum sets out local differences. Where local law gives you more rights, the local rule applies.

items.text: Can I read it in my language?
items.detail: It is available in [languages] in the Policy guide. [Where local law requires: the [language] version prevails.]

items.text: What happens if I don't acknowledge it by the due date?
items.detail: You'll get reminders at 14 and 30 days, and your manager will be told at 30 days. Acknowledging confirms you received and read the policy. The policy applies from its effective date whether or not you acknowledge it.

items.text: Does this change my pay, benefits, leave balance or contract?
items.detail: [Approved answer.] If it does, you will receive [individual notice] at least [notice period] before the change.

items.text: Were employee representatives consulted?
items.detail: [Germany: The works council agreed the policy on [date]. China: The policy was discussed with employees and the union through democratic procedure on [dates]. Vietnam: The union was consulted and the internal labor regulations were registered on [date]. Taiwan: The work rules were filed and approved on [date]. Elsewhere: Not required.]

items.text: Where can I see exactly what changed?
items.detail: A summary of changes is at the top of the policy page, and the previous version is available from [HR help channel] on request.

items.text: I think the policy conflicts with my contract or local practice. What should I do?
items.detail: Contact your HRBP. Where your contract or local law gives you a better term, that term applies.

items.text: How do I raise a concern about how the policy is applied?
items.detail: Talk to your manager or HRBP, or use [Speak Up channel], which allows anonymous reports where local law permits. Retaliation for raising a concern in good faith is prohibited.

items.text: Send reminders to employees who have not acknowledged at day 14 and day 30.
Send managers a list of their team members not yet acknowledged at day 30; escalate to the regional HR lead at day 45.
Review questions from HR channels weekly for the first month and update the FAQ when the same question appears three times.
Report the acknowledgment rate by jurisdiction in the weekly status report until it reaches 98%.

notes: Lead with what changes for the employee and what they need to do. The reason for the change comes second and fits in two sentences.
Managers hear it first. A manager who learns about a policy from the all-employee email cannot answer questions or reinforce it.
The protected-rights paragraph is fixed text approved by Legal. Do not shorten or translate it freely; use the approved translation in each language.
Localize, don't just translate: local effective dates, consultation statements and prevailing-language lines differ by country and must match the approval record.
Do not send the email in a country until its local gates are complete. In China and Vietnam the email and acknowledgment are part of the publication evidence.
Keep the FAQ alive for a month. Repeated questions show where the policy or the summary is unclear and feed the wave retrospective.

countryNotes.us: Keep the protected-rights paragraph (NLRA Section 7, SEC whistleblower rights) in every US version, and do not use mandatory meetings to discuss union matters.
countryNotes.us-ca: Provide translated versions where 2 CCR 11023 applies (EEO and harassment policies, languages spoken by 10%+ of a facility). SB 399's captive-audience ban is enjoined (2025), but keep briefings to policy content.
countryNotes.us-co: Keep confidentiality-related wording consistent with the POWR Act, and give HFWA-related notices in English and any language spoken by 5%+ of the workforce.
countryNotes.us-nc: Where the policy reduces pay, PTO or bonus terms, the email can serve as the written notice, so send it at least one full pay period before the effective date and keep proof of delivery.
countryNotes.us-tx: Use the standard US version; offer a Spanish version where part of the workforce prefers it.
countryNotes.us-wa: Briefings must not become mandatory meetings on political, religious or union topics (RCW 49.44.250), and confidentiality-related policies keep the Silenced No More carve-out.
countryNotes.ca: English for Ontario and BC; French for Quebec-based staff (Bill 96). For Ontario written policies required under the ESA, the email can serve as the copy given to employees if the policy is attached or linked (verify).
countryNotes.de: Send a German or bilingual version, mention the works council agreement where the topic is co-determined, and agree the timing with the works council; it may want to send its own message alongside.
countryNotes.il: Send Hebrew versions (Arabic where needed) Sunday to Thursday, avoiding holiday weeks.
countryNotes.in: English is standard for the email; display statutory policy content bilingually and avoid Diwali week and state holidays.
countryNotes.tw: Send a Traditional Chinese version and, where the change is in the work rules, state the authority approval date and where the rules are posted.
countryNotes.cn: Send a Simplified Chinese version and keep delivery and acknowledgment records: they are part of the publication step of democratic procedure and the evidence for later disciplinary use.
countryNotes.vn: Send a Vietnamese version stating the registration of the internal labor regulations and the date they take effect, and post the regulations at the workplace.

templates.name: Wave retrospective guide
templates.purpose: A two-hour, blameless retrospective at the end of each wave that uses data and the experience of owners, approvers and country teams to agree no more than five changes for the next wave. It turns delivery problems into concrete changes to the plan, templates, approval chains and ways of working.
templates.audience: Neutral facilitator (for example the HR Change and Communications lead or a trained facilitator outside the PMO); workstream leads; regional and country HR leads; a sample of item owners and approvers; Employment counsel; PMO (presents data and owns actions).
templates.when: Final week of each wave: Wave 1 by 11 February 2027 (required for M08), Wave 2 by 13 May 2027, Wave 3 by 12 August 2027; Wave 4 learning is captured in the close-out report by 1 October 2027. A shorter 60-minute Mobilize retrospective is held after M04.
templates.owner: Program management office (CC4), with HR Change and Communications (CC3) facilitating

items.text: Send the pulse survey to all item owners, approvers and country HR leads in the wave, with 3 business days to respond.

Build the data pack: planned versus actual time in each stage (target 2, 3, 2, 2 and 1 weeks), send-back rate in Review and Approve, approval wait time by step, overdue rate, country gate lead times planned versus actual, change requests raised, acknowledgment rates.
Review the actions from the previous retrospective and mark each done, in progress or dropped, with evidence.
Invite 12 to 16 people across workstreams and regions; hold a second session in APAC hours if needed.
For Wave 1, collect China, Taiwan and Vietnam input in writing by 4 February 2027, before the Lunar New Year and Tet freeze.

sections.title: Pulse survey
sections.intro: Anonymous, five questions, under 5 minutes. Results are shown in aggregate only.

items.text: How clear was the definition of done at each stage for your items? (1 to 5)
How well did the templates and Atlas pages help you do the work? (1 to 5) What would you change?
How long did approvals take compared with what you expected, and where did items wait longest?
Which country gate (consultation, translation, filing, posting) took longer than planned, and why?
What one thing should we start, stop and continue in the next wave?
Thanks for making time. This is a blameless review: we assume everyone did the best they could with what they knew and the time they had.
We're looking at the system, meaning the plan, templates, approval chains, tools and handoffs, not at individuals.
By the end we want at most five changes for [next wave], each with an owner and a date. Anything else goes on a list for later.
First, here's what we said we'd change after the last wave, and whether it worked.
What stands out in the stage times? Where did items spend longer than planned?
items.detail: Probes: Was it waiting or working time? Which workstreams or item types? Were drafts late or were reviews slow?

items.text: Where were items sent back, and what were the most common reasons?
items.detail: Probes: missing addenda, legal issues found late, inconsistency with another policy, incomplete templates. Could the issue have been caught earlier?

items.text: How did the country gates perform against plan?
items.detail: Probes: works council, democratic procedure, work rules filing, internal labor regulation registration, translation turnaround; which estimates were wrong and by how much.

items.text: What does the pulse survey tell us that the numbers don't?

sections.title: What worked and what didn't (0:35 to 1:10)

items.text: Discover: did the baseline and discovery workshops give drafters what they needed?
items.detail: Probes: were maps validated on time; did workshops capture the real process; what was missing when drafting started?

items.text: Draft and Review: what made drafting faster or slower, and did parallel review work?
items.detail: Probes: template fit, access to SMEs, legal turnaround, plain-language edits that caused rework.

items.text: Approve: where did approvals stall, and why?
items.detail: Probes: approver availability, delegation, 'all' steps waiting on one region, optional steps skipped without reasons, email approvals.

items.text: Go live: did communications, manager briefings and acknowledgments land?
items.detail: Probes: acknowledgment rate at day 30; questions received; local launch timing; evidence completeness.

items.text: Atlas and reporting: did the Master checklist, Approvals page and status report help or create extra work?
What should we keep doing exactly as it is?
For the top three problems, ask 'why' until you reach something we control.
items.detail: Stop at a cause the program can change: a template, a rule in the plan, an approver setup, a lead time, a resourcing decision.

items.text: What would we change, specifically, so this doesn't happen in the next wave?
items.detail: Each change must be concrete enough to check later, for example 'start Germany works council information at Draft, not Review'.

items.text: Vote: each person has three votes across the proposed changes. Which five do we commit to?
Who owns each change, and by when will it be in place?
items.detail: Changes to plan dates or scope need a change request (T-PM-CHANGE-REQUEST); template changes go to the PMO.

items.text: Read back the agreed changes, owners and dates, and the 'later' list.
Publish the retrospective summary on Project HQ within 2 business days: data highlights, agreed changes, later list.
Add each agreed change to the RAID log as an action and track it in the weekly status report until done.
Raise change requests for any plan or scope changes and update templates in the Templates page with a version note.
Add the lessons to the lessons register used for the close-out report (T-PM-CLOSEOUT).

notes: Keep it blameless. Name system causes (a template gap, a missing approver, an unrealistic lead time), not people. Individual performance issues go to the line manager, not the retrospective.
The facilitator should not be the HR Program Manager. The PMO presents data and owns actions but should not also steer the discussion about its own plan.
Bring numbers. Stage times against the 2-3-2-2-1 week plan, send-back reasons and gate lead times turn opinions into a shared picture.
Commit to five changes at most. Programs that agree twenty changes implement none.
Include country voices. Variance in local gates usually explains more schedule slippage than drafting speed.
Close the loop. Start each retrospective by reviewing the last one's actions; changes that were never made are themselves a finding.

countryNotes.us-nc: Capture whether the advance written notice for pay, PTO or bonus changes was planned early enough.
countryNotes.us-tx: Capture whether Texas worked well as a pilot site for US launches and what should be reused.
countryNotes.us-wa: Capture how quickly items were updated after Washington law changes and whether briefings stayed clear of the captive-audience rule.
countryNotes.ca: Capture whether separate Ontario and BC addenda worked, and any Quebec questions that arose.
countryNotes.de: Compare actual works council lead times with the plan and record what helped (early information, joint drafting, regular meetings), so the next wave's German schedule is realistic.
countryNotes.il: Capture Hebrew translation turnaround and the impact of holidays and reserve duty; hold the session Sunday to Thursday.
countryNotes.in: Capture lessons on bilingual displays, standing orders and changes to state rules, and offer a session time that suits Indian working hours.
countryNotes.tw: Record the work rules filing turnaround by authority and the impact of the Lunar New Year freeze on Wave 1.
countryNotes.cn: Record how long democratic procedure took, the acknowledgment rate achieved and the impact of the Lunar New Year freeze.
countryNotes.vn: Record the time from dossier submission to registration receipt, union consultation lessons and the impact of the Tet freeze.

It is the evidence for the handover milestone on 1 October 2027 (M17) and is approved by the steering committee at project close on 8 October 2027 (M18).

templates.when: Drafting starts 13 September 2027, after the attestation campaign launch (M15); data frozen 29 September 2027; handover sign-offs complete 1 October 2027 (M17); report approved 8 October 2027 (M18).
